findings.highlight: I figure she'd get suspicious if someone had sprinted up to the rooftop and was gasping for air for no good reason.
findings.evidenceJa: そっちの方が怪しいと思うんだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that a person who sprints to the roof for no reason would be the more suspicious party. The English instead makes Setsuna suspicious of that person, reversing who is making the judgment and losing his dry retort to her question.
findings.japanese:
何の理由もなく、
息も絶え絶えに屋上に駆け上がってくる人間がいたら、
そっちの方が怪しいと思うんだけど。
findings.todokanai: I figure she'd get suspicious if someone had sprinted up to the rooftop and was gasping for air for no good reason.

findings.highlight: A group as fantastic as this sounds too good to be true, doesn't it?
findings.evidenceJa: こんな幸せな締め方、ないんじゃないのか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether there could be any happier way to bring this moment—and what he has decided will be his final performance—to a close. The English invents a fantastic group and evaluates it as too good to be true, deleting the idea of an emotionally satisfying ending.
findings.japanese:
しかも最後の最後に綺麗なボーカルまでついて、
こんな幸せな締め方、ないんじゃないのか？
findings.todokanai: And right at the last minute, a beautiful singer appears. A group as fantastic as this sounds too good to be true, doesn't it?

findings.highlight: Don't just casually say that! You're making me feel uneasy here!
findings.evidenceJa: さり気なく一文字すり替えるなよ
findings.explanation: Chikashi has asked whether Haruki has an ate—a lead or prospect—and Haruki answers saa, “who knows,” changing a single sound. Chikashi explicitly protests that one-character substitution. The English retains only generic anxiety and erases the joke it is reacting to.
findings.japanese:
「さり気なく一文字すり替えるなよ！
思いっきり不安になるじゃないか！」
findings.todokanai: "Don't just casually say that! You're making me feel uneasy here!"

findings.highlight: I didn't think she would come all the way here to seriously respond to my crazy invitation.
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで真剣に反応するとは思いもしなかった
findings.explanation: ここまで measures the degree of Setsuna's seriousness: Haruki never expected her to take his outrageous invitation this seriously. The English misreads it spatially as her coming “all the way here.”
findings.japanese:
俺の、あまりに突拍子もない誘いに、
ここまで真剣に反応するとは思いもしなかった。
findings.todokanai: I didn't think she would come all the way here to seriously respond to my crazy invitation.

findings.highlight: I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしなんかにやれるのか、今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか
findings.explanation: Setsuna separates three questions: whether she is capable, whether the person she currently is has the right or standing to do it, and whether she wants to. The English turns the second question into another question of ability, erasing the normative self-doubt that later makes her “two-to-one” reversal meaningful.
findings.japanese:
「わたしなんかにやれるのか、
今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、
そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか」
findings.todokanai: "I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it."

findings.highlight: I'll lend you my shoulder as well. If it's only for crying anyway…
findings.evidenceJa: なんなら胸貸してやってもいいぞ。…泣くだけなら
findings.explanation: Chikashi offers Haruki his chest, then hastily limits the offer to crying. That bodily intimacy is why Haruki immediately calls the suggestion disgusting. Replacing chest with the conventional English shoulder removes the comic setup while leaving both the qualification and Haruki's reaction stranded.
findings.japanese:
「なんなら胸貸してやってもいいぞ。
…泣くだけなら」
findings.todokanai: "I'll lend you my shoulder as well. If it's only for crying anyway…"

findings.highlight: Past Minami-Suetsugu Station, the entertainment district for the students; the second closest station to school, Suetsugu-chou Station, shows an unchanging scenery.
findings.evidenceJa: 学校から二番目に近い末次町駅前は、学生たちの歓楽街を最寄り駅の南末次に譲り
findings.explanation: Suetsugucho is the second-closest station to school; the nearest station, Minami-Suetsugu, has taken the student entertainment district for itself. The English makes Minami-Suetsugu something the narration moves past, obscures which station owns the district, and leaves the sentence structurally broken.
findings.japanese:
学校から二番目に近い末次町駅前は、
学生たちの歓楽街を最寄り駅の南末次に譲り、
来るたび代わり映えのしない光景を映し出している。
findings.todokanai: Past Minami-Suetsugu Station, the entertainment district for the students; the second closest station to school, Suetsugu-chou Station, shows an unchanging scenery.

findings.highlight: The diligent, braided girl who does her best to tend to the grocery store front.
findings.evidenceJa: スーパーの店先で、一生懸命品出しに励む三つ編みの少女
findings.explanation: This deliberately repeats the earlier image of the braided girl diligently stocking goods at the supermarket entrance, now revealing that background figure as Setsuna. “Tend to the grocery store front” changes the action and weakens the repeated wording that performs the reveal.
findings.japanese:
スーパーの店先で、
一生懸命品出しに励む三つ編みの少女。
findings.todokanai: The diligent, braided girl who does her best to tend to the grocery store front.

findings.highlight: Looks like she went to get some leftover food from the grocery store… How thrifty of her.
findings.evidenceJa: どうやらスーパーの残り物を貰ってきたらしい。………なんという生活感
findings.explanation: Setsuna appears to have been given the supermarket's leftovers; Haruki is struck by her vivid air of ordinary domestic life. The English turns receiving leftovers into going to obtain them and replaces domestic lived-in texture with a judgment that she is thrifty.
findings.japanese:
どうやらスーパーの残り物を貰ってきたらしい。
………なんという生活感。
findings.todokanai: Looks like she went to get some leftover food from the grocery store… How thrifty of her.

findings.highlight: I was a bit taken aback when I first talked to you, Kitahara-kun.
findings.evidenceJa: 初めて北原くんとお話ししたときのこと、ちょっと引っかかってたんだ
findings.explanation: Something about their first conversation had continued to nag at or puzzle Setsuna, leading into the remarks she now quotes. “Was taken aback” makes it a momentary surprise during the conversation and loses the lingering question that motivates this exchange.
findings.japanese:
「初めて北原くんとお話ししたときのこと、
ちょっと引っかかってたんだ」
findings.todokanai: "I was a bit taken aback when I first talked to you, Kitahara-kun."

findings.highlight: I find myself not altogether disliking the look of this particular braided and bespectacled girl before me.
findings.evidenceJa: 今、目の前にいるこの三つ編み眼鏡少女は、思いっきりアリだと思ってしまえる
findings.explanation: After saying braided girls with glasses are not especially his type, Haruki concedes that the girl before him is emphatically ari—absolutely a yes. The English replaces that strong attraction with the evasive and much weaker “not altogether disliking.”
findings.japanese:
やはりというか、さすがというか、
今、目の前にいるこの三つ編み眼鏡少女は、
思いっきりアリだと思ってしまえる。
findings.todokanai: But as cliche as it may sound, I find myself not altogether disliking the look of this particular braided and bespectacled girl before me.

findings.highlight: the beautiful face behind those glasses felt out of place, to say the least.
findings.evidenceJa: その眼鏡の奥の素顔は、細かいことを気にする俺にとって、格好のチェック対象だった
findings.explanation: Her bare face behind the glasses became an ideal object of scrutiny for detail-obsessed Haruki, explaining how he eventually recognized her disguise. The English invents “beautiful,” says the face felt out of place, and deletes the observational habit that causes the recognition.
findings.japanese:
その眼鏡の奥の素顔は、
細かいことを気にする俺にとって、
格好のチェック対象だった。
findings.todokanai: And for someone like me who paid attention to small details, the beautiful face behind those glasses felt out of place, to say the least.

findings.highlight: Even though I've been here like this for a year now.
findings.evidenceJa: それこそ一年の頃からずっと
findings.explanation: Setsuna has used this disguise ever since her first year at school, not merely for one year. As a third-year student, the English shortens the history of her double life by roughly half.
findings.japanese:
「今のわたしの正体が見破られたの、今日が初めて。
それこそ一年の頃からずっと、だったのに」
findings.todokanai: "Today's the first time anyone's managed to recognize me like this. Even though I've been here like this for a year now."

findings.highlight: After all, Ogiso has resolved to talk about it with a nobody like me…
findings.evidenceJa: 小木曽が、他の誰にでもないこの俺に、大きな覚悟を持って話してくれるんだから
findings.explanation: Haruki is struck that Setsuna has resolved to tell this to him and no one else—to me, of all people. The English replaces that exclusive act of trust with unsupported self-abasement, calling him “a nobody.”
findings.japanese:
小木曽が、他の誰にでもないこの俺に、
大きな覚悟を持って話してくれるんだから…
findings.todokanai: After all, Ogiso has resolved to talk about it with a nobody like me…

findings.highlight: I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…
findings.evidenceJa: 後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she piled one act of keeping up appearances upon another to preserve the image. “Did so many things” deletes the accumulating pretense that trapped her inside the school persona.
findings.japanese:
「そうなると、
後はそのイメージを守るために見栄に見栄を重ねて…」
findings.todokanai: "When that happened, I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…"

findings.highlight: Having heard her somewhat lackluster confession
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで微妙な打ち明け話をされると
findings.explanation: 微妙 describes a confession awkwardly poised between grave and trivial, which is why Haruki cannot decide whether to press or retreat. “Lackluster” instead dismisses Setsuna's confession as dull or unimpressive.
findings.japanese:
なにしろ、ここまで微妙な打ち明け話をされると、
押していいのか引くべきなのか判断できない。
findings.todokanai: Having heard her somewhat lackluster confession, I'm on the fence about whether I should push onward or pull back.

findings.highlight: Ogiso gives me a cheerful look, making me wonder whether she'd noticed I was hesitating just now.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなふうに逡巡してる隙に、小木曽は正体がバレてスッキリしてしまったのか、結構晴れ晴れとした顔で立ち上がる
findings.explanation: While Haruki hesitates, Setsuna stands looking relieved—perhaps because having her identity exposed has cleared the air. The English invents her noticing his hesitation and makes that the focus of her expression.
findings.japanese:
そんなふうに逡巡してる隙に、
小木曽は正体がバレてスッキリしてしまったのか、
結構晴れ晴れとした顔で立ち上がる。
findings.todokanai: Ogiso gives me a cheerful look, making me wonder whether she'd noticed I was hesitating just now.

findings.highlight: My mom makes dinner three times a week.
findings.evidenceJa: お母さんも週三でパートなの
findings.explanation: Setsuna says her mother also works part-time three days a week. The English turns the mother's employment schedule into a dinner rota.
findings.japanese:
「お母さんも週三でパートなの。
それにそろそろ弟がお腹空かせて帰ってくる頃だし」
findings.todokanai: "My mom makes dinner three times a week. Also, my hungry younger brother is coming home soon."

findings.highlight: You shouldn't easily believe in cool-headed people who take advantage of others' weaknesses, or selfish people who don't consider others' circumstances.
findings.evidenceJa: 人の弱みに付け込む冷徹さと、人の事情を考えない卑劣さを持つ人間を、そんなに簡単に信じていいわけがないって
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns himself as one person possessing both the coldness to exploit weakness and the baseness to ignore another's circumstances. The English generalizes this into advice about two kinds of “people,” softens 冷徹 into “cool-headed,” and turns 卑劣 into ordinary selfishness.
findings.japanese:
人の弱みに付け込む冷徹さと、
人の事情を考えない卑劣さを持つ人間を、
そんなに簡単に信じていいわけがないって。
findings.todokanai: You shouldn't easily believe in cool-headed people who take advantage of others' weaknesses, or selfish people who don't consider others' circumstances.

findings.highlight: being a business district that doesn't sleep, even in the dead of night.
findings.evidenceJa: 深夜遅くまで眠らない繁華街、南末次
findings.explanation: Minami-Suetsugu is a nightlife or entertainment district that stays awake late into the night. Calling it a business district gives the rendezvous the wrong urban setting and atmosphere.
findings.japanese:
末次町とは違い、
深夜遅くまで眠らない繁華街、南末次。
findings.todokanai: Minami-Suetsugu is different from Suetsugu-chou, being a business district that doesn't sleep, even in the dead of night.

findings.highlight: Just the two of us, in the night of the business district…
findings.evidenceJa: 夜の繁華街。二人きりの待ち合わせ
findings.explanation: The repeated setup is a nighttime rendezvous for two in an entertainment district, with the suggestive associations that creates. “The night of the business district” is both the wrong setting and defective English.
findings.japanese:
夜の繁華街。
二人きりの待ち合わせ。
findings.todokanai: Just the two of us, in the night of the business district…

findings.highlight: next will be the usual ones, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 次はいつもの定番を流してみようかな
findings.explanation: Setsuna muses that she will put on her usual standards next. The English converts her self-directed decision into a confirmation question to Haruki, weakening the scene's joke that she controls the entire karaoke session without consulting him.
findings.japanese:
「ええと…とりあえず新曲一通り行ったから、
次はいつもの定番を流してみようかな」
findings.todokanai: "Umm… since we went through the new songs for the time being, next will be the usual ones, right?"

findings.highlight: The business district. The two of us alone, in the middle of the night.
findings.evidenceJa: 夜の繁華街。二人きりの待ち合わせ
findings.explanation: The narration repeats its deliberately suggestive “nighttime entertainment district; a rendezvous for two” setup immediately before the karaoke punchline. The English again substitutes a business district and changes a rendezvous into generic physical solitude.
findings.japanese:
夜の繁華街。
二人きりの待ち合わせ。
findings.todokanai: The business district. The two of us alone, in the middle of the night.

findings.highlight: Did I disappoint you?
findings.evidenceJa: 退いた？
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether this side of her has put Haruki off or made him recoil. “Disappoint” makes her worry that she failed an expectation rather than that her intensity repelled him.
findings.todokanai: "…Did I disappoint you?"

findings.highlight: It's such a waste if you can't even get through ten songs in two hours, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: ２時間で１０曲歌えなかったりすると悔しいでしょ
findings.explanation: Setsuna says it is frustrating or galling not to manage ten songs in two hours; Haruki immediately repeats those emotional words in disbelief. “A waste” changes the emotion into an efficiency judgment and weakens his reaction.
findings.japanese: ２時間で１０曲歌えなかったりすると悔しいでしょ？」
findings.todokanai: It's such a waste if you can't even get through ten songs in two hours, you know?"

findings.highlight: And if you start singing right after the previous song ends, you can fit in about five more.
findings.evidenceJa: 歌い終わってすぐに演奏ストップすれば、さらに５曲くらい稼げるし
findings.explanation: Setsuna stops the accompaniment as soon as she finishes singing, skipping each remaining instrumental outro to squeeze in five more songs. The English instead has her start singing after a song has already ended, which is ordinary karaoke sequencing and loses the obsessive trick.
findings.japanese:
「その点、一人なら２時間あれば３０曲は歌えるし。
歌い終わってすぐに演奏ストップすれば、
さらに５曲くらい稼げるし」
findings.todokanai: "On that note, one person can sing 30 songs in two hours. And if you start singing right after the previous song ends, you can fit in about five more."

findings.highlight: when I heard a song I'm good at… not to mention it being my favorite song
findings.evidenceJa: 自分のレパートリーの…しかも一番のお気に入りが流れてきちゃったら
findings.explanation: The song was part of Setsuna's repertoire and, moreover, her favorite. レパートリー does not assert that she is especially good at it; the English invents a skill claim where she is explaining irresistible familiarity and attachment.
findings.japanese:
「だから、自分のレパートリーの…
しかも一番のお気に入りが流れてきちゃったら、
我慢なんかしてられる訳、ないの」
findings.todokanai: "That's why, when I heard a song I'm good at… not to mention it being my favorite song, there was no way I could hold it in."

findings.highlight: So that's… the reason.
findings.evidenceJa: あれは………ガチか
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that her rooftop performance was genuine—the real thing, not a momentary lapse. The English replaces that assessment with a generic causal conclusion.
findings.japanese: あれは………ガチか。
findings.todokanai: So that's… the reason.

findings.highlight: Ogiso puts on a delighted, enchanting face.
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に嬉しそうな恍惚の表情を浮かべた
findings.explanation: Setsuna's expression is rapt or ecstatic as she relives singing with them. “Enchanting” describes how attractive her face is to an observer, redirecting her inward musical ecstasy into conventional feminine allure.
findings.japanese:
あの時のことを思い出すべく目を閉じた小木曽は、
本当に嬉しそうな恍惚の表情を浮かべた。
findings.todokanai: After closing her eyes to remember that moment, Ogiso puts on a delighted, enchanting face.

findings.highlight: I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしなんかにやれるのか、今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか
findings.explanation: The earlier three-part question is repeated here: ability, whether the person she currently is has the right to do it, and desire. The English again collapses the normative second question into ability, damaging the exact repetition on which Setsuna now bases her two-to-one vote.
findings.japanese:
「わたしなんかにやれるのか、
今のわたしがやってもいいことなのか、
そもそも、わたしはやりたいのか」
findings.todokanai: "I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it."

findings.highlight: I thought I couldn't do it. I thought I couldn't do it the way I am now.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしなんかにできないと思った。今のわたしがやってもいいこととも思えなかった
findings.explanation: Setsuna explicitly answers two different questions: she thought she could not do it, and she thought it was not something the present version of herself was entitled or fit to do. The English repeats inability twice, erasing one of the two votes she is about to overrule with desire.
findings.japanese:
「わたしなんかにできないと思った。
今のわたしがやってもいいこととも思えなかった」
findings.todokanai: "I thought I couldn't do it. I thought I couldn't do it the way I am now."

findings.highlight: as if to cover up various important things about herself.
findings.evidenceJa: 今決まった、色々と重要な事実を覆い隠すかのように
findings.explanation: Setsuna's playful gesture seems designed to cover the various important facts just decided—above all her reversal and participation—not biographical facts about herself. The English attaches the modifier to the wrong subject matter.
findings.japanese:
ほんの一瞬、ぺろりと舌を出した小木曽は、
今決まった、色々と重要な事実を覆い隠すかのように、
マイクを取り、立ち上がった。
findings.todokanai: Ogiso sticks out her tongue for an instant, taking the microphone and standing up, as if to cover up various important things about herself.

findings.highlight: Despite my face burning… I really am breaking out in a cold sweat.
findings.evidenceJa: 顔は火照ってるのに出るのは…やっぱり熱い汗
findings.explanation: Earlier Haruki called it cold sweat despite his flushed face. After Setsuna joins and tells him he now knows everything about her, the narration corrects itself: this time it is, after all, hot sweat. Todokanai TL says cold sweat again, reversing the emotional and verbal payoff.
findings.japanese: …顔は火照ってるのに出るのは…やっぱり熱い汗。
findings.todokanai: …Despite my face burning… I really am breaking out in a cold sweat.
